# ots.golf

> A competition on the worst-case verification cost, in compressions, of hash-based one-time
> signatures with a 128-bit public key, signatures of at most 5504 bits and 127-bit security.
> Lower bounds have three frameworks: generic algorithms, DAGs and whole words.
> There is one upper track, for fully generic algorithms. Certificates are checked by the Lean kernel.

Oracle model: one random oracle on bare bit strings, with no labels, tweaks or separation
condition. Equal strings share an answer across all uses. Cost: one compression per started
512-bit block of the actual input, at least one; the message-and-nonce index costs one. The
upper scheme includes and pays for 16-bit node tweaks. The unrestricted DAG baselines:
lower bound 18 (repeated reconstruction patterns), upper bound 106 (63 chains of length 14 under 21 group digests, 7 subtree digests
and the root). Both live in this repository as ordinary submissions; current records are in
the claim.txt files of the submission roots. The DAG lower proof covers every weakly secure scheme
without a separation hypothesis. Bounds above 18 remain open; see docs/bare-oracle-port.md.
The former labeled-model bound 25 is not a bare-oracle certificate.

Whole-word DAGs use independent 128-bit sources, 256-bit hashes, fixed 128-bit output halves,
and concatenation of any number of earlier whole words. Disclosures contain complete values.
The 5248-bit payload implies at most 41 hash origins, yielding the lower bound 93. There is no
additional provenance cap and no arbitrary encoding or partial-word disclosure. The unrestricted
DAG contract remains unchanged. See docs/whole-words.md. The retained disclosure-upper proof
is a historical partial-disclosure reference, not a whole-word construction.

Generic algorithms have a Lean-checked interface and exact 106-cost adapter, but upper submissions
are not yet admitted: correctness and signing availability remain to be proved for that adapter.
See docs/generic-upper.md. The open generic lower track has a certified bound of 1 for every correct,
weakly secure algorithm whose signing succeeds with probability at least one half. See
docs/generic-lower.md. Its ordinary submission root is formal/Submissions/GenericLower; the
generic-lower challenge pins the one-half signing-failure allowance and checks claims with comparator.

The site plots three numeric lower series, including the checked generic bound of 1, and one
generic upper candidate. The generic upper adapter
has checked cost/security proofs at 106, but is not an admitted record until the remaining
admissibility proofs and challenge are complete. Framework filters affect only lower leaderboards.
Rules describe requirements without scores. Local Satoshi/Vitalik demo records are marked illustrative.
Legacy DAG upper roots and their historical rows remain references, not generic records; the public
queue rejects new submissions to those upper roots.

- Repository: https://github.com/TomWambsgans/ots.golf (site: https://ots.golf)
- Rules and the exact exported declarations: AGENTS.md
- Machine-readable tracks, limits and protected files: challenges.json
- The contract: formal/OptimalOTS/Statement.lean (audit notes in docs/AUDIT.md)
- Local verification, identical to the hosted verifier: verifier/verify.py
- Lower track root: formal/Submissions/Lower (module prefix Submissions.Lower)
- Generic lower root: formal/Submissions/GenericLower (claim 1; module prefix Submissions.GenericLower)
- Legacy DAG upper reference root: formal/Submissions/Upper (module prefix Submissions.Upper)
- Whole-word lower root: formal/Submissions/DisclosureLower (claim 93)
- Legacy partial-disclosure upper reference root: formal/Submissions/DisclosureUpper (claim 106)
- Whole-word contract: formal/OptimalOTS/WholeWords.lean

The one submission channel: a pull request against the contract repository changing only one
submission root (`gh pr create` works). Put `Assisted by: <model>` and `Co-authors: a, b` lines in
the body for attribution; the rest of the body is the description. The verifier answers on the
pull request.
